estimand: NJ–PA mean change in FTE headcount among observed complete restaurant pairs
assignment_narrative: Known statewide NJ floor increase, compared with surveyed PA establishments; observational comparison, not random assignment.
interpretation_boundary: Supported descriptive change contrast; conditional ATT only under unverified counterfactual, anticipation, spillover and selection assumptions.

diagnostics.finding: State residence and statutory policy timing define treatment; no random-assignment claim.
Both states and all four chains present; source-row keys preserve duplicate sheet identifier.
Only two policy jurisdictions; HC1/OLS/bootstrap condition on state paths and cannot estimate statewide shock uncertainty.
NJ legislative archive schedules April 1, 1992; baseline instrument January–March and observed post dates November–December.
PA restaurants are observed contemporaneously but comparable untreated employment changes cannot be verified.
Increase legislated before baseline; no data identify anticipatory employment response.
One baseline wave precludes pretrend diagnostics; assumption not empirically verified.
Cross-border labor/product substitution and chain wage spillovers are not observed.
Single adoption date; no staggered TWFE weighting problem. Chain omissions and initial-wage diagnostic reported descriptively.
